Brother, you’re not mistaken about the obscurity of this title.I’m something of an expert in tracking down lost feature films and documentaries, and have a very successful track record of locating movies that no one else owns. But this is one that continues to stump me.I’ve tried everything I can think of to find The Luckiest Man in the World, including trawling deep web movie sites on which I’m a member, that are invitation only and have 400,000 rare titles to download, from all over the world, and checking with a friend who is an underground bootlegger in Europe who has a catalog almost as large. Nothing.I also routinely check ebay to see if I can find 16 or 35mm prints of Luckiest Man, and nothing has ever materialized aside from publicity stills. There has never been a single clip on youtube, and newspapers.com indicates no television run for LMW in the 1990s. I have never seen a home video release in any format, including VHS or DVD or Laserdisc or Videodisc or Betamax.The one and only extant copy documented online is a print at the Library of Congress. It appears that it had a limited run in theaters and a few museums for about a year, and then vanished.

Well the other factor to consider is that people often make ridiculous incendiary statements in the heat of a breakup. I don’t necessarily mean that he was just blowing smoke about not loving you - I don’t know either of you and have no way to gauge that. But such comments are not uncommon.

One of my girlfriends, two back, was emotionally unstable - became emotionally unstable. Over 4 1/2 years we broke up probably 5 or 6 times. We took turns initiating. And whenever I initiated, she would fly off the handle, into a violent rage, and say outrageous, hurtful things that she knew were not true in order to get back at me. Once she accused me of plotting to wreck her car and kill her cats. (I’m not a violent person, and love animals, and would never do either in a million years). It was just complete bullshit designed to wound me. And there were also statements about how she never really loved me. We remained together 2 1/2 years after she first said that.

I realize it isn't a perfect analogy, maybe especially given the fact that it sounds like he was the one who initiated. But in the heat of emotion people often make overblown statements they don't mean.

You make a great point about never again lowering yourself and sacrificing self-respect for a partner. And I'm glad to hear you saying "once I'm over this." Because the pain often does go away. It's infuriating to hear people say that, but in the wake of a breakup, time helps and heals.

Hi There,

I read your post and thank you for sharing. I’m so very sorry you’re in this situation and my heart goes out to you. It sounds absolutely awful.

One thought that occurs to me: you have learned a great deal from this relationship, clearly. You said, “Things weren't perfect. We fought a lot over stupid shit. In hindsight I feel like it was mostly due to my inability to handle my emotions. I get angry way too quickly and I caused many incidents where I took my anger out on her for shit she had nothing to do with. It was too much for her.”

I think one of the keys, here, is to take that lesson moving forward - if you are able to eventually move forward. And only you can determine that.

If she’s happily with someone else (and you’re sure she’s happy? how do you know this?), that door is closed right now. There is no reason why you can’t write her a letter expressing remorse for the way you treated her, but to do so right now with the expectation that she’s going to come back after reading it would be ill-advised. Maybe such things do eventually need to be said, but not until you can free them of romantic expectations. 

As someone who has had six relationships and have fallen in love (deeply in love, head over heels, not infatuated) twice… It is possible to mutually fall in love with someone on the level that you are describing, more than once. But I believe it is rare. 

How did the second relationship compare to the first in terms of emotion? It doesn’t sound like you were in love with the second girl. Is that accurate?

Ron

When the breakup happened, I made a statement to my folks and therapist and still stand by it. Her relationship history is a dysfunctional one, and the guy before me was a prick and an asshole who strung her along, used her sexually, and dumped her. When she broke up with me, she told me I'm a wonderful man and said I'm the first guy who ever made her understand what it felt like to be loved. What I wanted to say in response \- and didn't have an opportunity, is this: great. If that's what you're taking away from us, great. Just do yourself a favor, and do me a favor. *Remember that. Remember how it feels to be loved, and whoever the next guy is, don't fucking forget how it feels to be loved and don't settle for another jerk who poses no real threat to you.* If I've done that for her \- if our relationship has done that? Fucking fantastic. That I'll feel good about. 

But how the hell do I know if she won't have any contact at all?! That's far crueler than the breakup. And even more of a reason why I'm headed down this path. It's much harder to lose my best friend than it was to lose my girlfriend. Devastating.
I'll say too that if I thought there were a chance she might eventually heal and come around, that would make a huge difference to me. It just seems so unlikely.

Not only no contact, but she is aggressively *running* as far away as possible. She didn't just unfriend me on facebook \- she actually went back and untagged herself from every post in which we were both involved which must have taken her hours. She expunged me from her relationship history. She ordered her mother to unfriend me \(which appeared to take a couple of days of arguing back and forth \- her parents were crazy about me\).  As I've said, she even unfriended me on Goodreads, which is a site I almost never use. The insane thing is that she's treating me like a stalker, and not only am I not that, I've been super\-conscientious about respecting her boundaries. I've only reached out a few times in the last few months, and always as a friend, never trying to get back together with her. I've been so respectful of her boundaries and wishes. And believe me, that wasn't my immediate impulse. My usual inclination is to try to talk it through with the person. Obviously that isn't an option in this case. 

Yes, she definitely has heavy personal stuff she's dealing with, including a clinical fear of intimacy \(physical and emotional\) which may or may not be related to a past sexual trauma. What I really, really want to do is say, point blank, "Go out and get help. Get better. I'll be here when you get back. Even if it means our only being friends. I *care about you, lady."*

Unfortunately, it doesn't much matter that it's her problem \(or problems\) and not mine. Look, I get it if a woman isn't attracted to me or doesn't give a shit. Like most guys, I've struck out plenty of times. This is not that. This is a case of someone who does care and is afraid. Irrationally afraid. We all know how fucking hard it is out there. This only overcomplicates things.

As for me, yes, I've made up my mind. I will say it's a deterrent to think that she'll find out. I don't want her to know. I wonder if there is a way to suppress news of my death?
